summary: --full's dependent-sync resumability (internal/cli/sync.go: planDependentSync, runDependentFanOut) is a two-tier design: a sweep cursor (sync_state key "<resource>:full_progress") that advances UNCONDITIONALLY by however many fresh (non-backlog) ids a batch attempted, regardless of any of their outcomes, plus a separately persisted failed-id backlog (sync_state key "<resource>:full_failed", a comma-joined id list stored in the cursor field) that gets retry priority on every subsequent call until each id succeeds. dependentSyncPlan carries the bookkeeping both halves need (fullOffsetKey/fullOffsetBase/fullSweepCount for the cursor, fullFailedKey/fullBacklogAll for the backlog) computed at planning time but NOT persisted until runDependentFanOut confirms plan.ids was actually fetched. The backlog recomputation formula is: (old backlog minus ids attempted this call) union (ids that failed this call, from either origin) -- this correctly retains untried backlog entries, drops backlog entries that just succeeded, and adds newly-failed ids, all in one pass. Candidate ordering puts the backlog first for retry priority, BUT capping under --max-parents reserves at least half the cap (rounding up) for the sweep unconditionally regardless of backlog size, with any unused backlog budget handed back to the sweep -- a naive candidates[:maxParents] slice would let a backlog >= the cap consume the entire budget every call, re-wedging the sweep by a different mechanism. The two sync_state rows (cursor and backlog) are written together via SaveSyncStatePair (internal/store/store.go), one SQL transaction, not two independent SaveSyncState calls -- so a crash or a single write failure between them can never leave the two checkpoints out of sync with each other. Any future dependent that adds --full offset tracking must use this same two-tier shape (unconditional sweep + separate backlog + reserved sweep budget under capping + atomic paired persistence), never make the sweep's advancement conditional on any batch's success/failure and never let backlog-first ordering go uncapped -- four different conditional/ordering variants were each found broken by live review (see reason).
reason: Found across four consecutive rounds of Greptile's automated review on the upstream PR splitting this branch's work (mvanhorn/printing-press-library#1773 and #1774), each catching a real edge case in the previous round's fix to the SAME mechanism. Round 1: the original implementation advanced the durable offset for every planned id before a single network/store operation ran, so ANY failure anywhere in a batch left the offset advanced past ids that were never actually fetched, silently skipping them until the next full pass wrapped around. Round 2 (gate advancement on zero failures in the whole batch): fixed round 1's exact case, but a parent that fails CONSISTENTLY (not transiently) would then permanently pin the sweep at the start of its own window, blocking every id after it in the pass indefinitely. Round 2.5 (advance past the leading run of successes, stopping at the first failure's position): fixed the trailing/scattered-failure cases from round 2's regression, but a chronically-failing id that sorts FIRST in its window still pinned the sweep at that exact position forever -- Round 3's finding, which prompted the two-tier redesign (unconditional sweep cursor + separate backlog) that replaced all the conditional-advancement variants at once. Round 4 then found two problems IN that redesign itself: (a) backlog-first candidate ordering with no reserved sweep budget meant a backlog >= --max-parents would consume the whole cap every call, starving the sweep exactly as badly as the original bug -- fixed by reserving at least half the cap for the sweep unconditionally; (b) the sweep-cursor and backlog sync_state rows were written via two independent SaveSyncState calls with both errors discarded, so a crash between them or either write failing alone could leave the two checkpoints permanently inconsistent with each other while the command still reported success -- fixed by SaveSyncStatePair, one transaction for both rows.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test and verify_skill.py all green (govulncheck not run locally, no dependency changes); go test -race scoped to every dependent-fan-out test confirms the failedIDs/backlog bookkeeping introduces no data race. Six end-to-end regression tests drive the real fetch/store path (not planDependentSync in isolation, which can't observe fetch failures): TestFullSyncOffsetDoesNotAdvancePastAPartialBatchFailure (round 1's original case). TestFullSyncOffsetSweepNeverWedgesOnAChronicallyFailingFirstID (round 3's exact case -- 5 ids, --max-parents 2, the first id fails on every one of 4 consecutive calls; asserts the sweep still reaches ids 3, 4, and 5). TestFullSyncOffsetFailedIDGetsBacklogPriorityAcrossCalls (a middle-of-batch chronic failure reappears FIRST on the next call). TestFullSyncOffsetLargeBacklogDoesNotStarveSweep (round 4a -- seeds a 3-id backlog against a --max-parents 2 cap and asserts the plan still includes a fresh sweep id, not just backlog entries). TestSaveSyncStatePair_WritesBothRowsTogether (round 4b, store package -- confirms both sync_state rows land with the values passed in one call). TestPlanDependentSync_FullResumesAcrossCallsAndWrapsAfterACompletePass and TestPlanDependentSync_DryRunDoesNotPersistFullOffset (pre-existing coverage) updated to model the new plan-then-commit-on-success shape via the commitFullOffset test helper. An independent code-review pass and live testing against a real account (round 5, requested explicitly because three straight rounds of Greptile-only iteration risked over-fitting to the automated checker) are pending as of this patch.
